why: Before the single value, every pair starts at an even index; after it, pairs start at odd indices. So 'nums[i] != nums[i ^ 1]' (with i even) flips from false to true exactly at the single element, a first-true search on a derived predicate.
hints: Look at the indices of the pairs to the left of the single value, then to the right. What changes?
For an even index i, nums[i] == nums[i + 1] holds left of the single value and fails from it onwards. Binary search only even indices for the first failure.
lo, hi = 0, n - 1; mid -= mid % 2; if nums[mid] == nums[mid + 1]: lo = mid + 2 else hi = mid. Return nums[lo]. O(log n).
pitfalls: Keep mid even, otherwise the pair test compares the wrong neighbours.
XOR of all values gives the answer in O(n) but ignores the logarithmic requirement.
